name: Erastus
role: City treasurer of Corinth and Paul's helper
whenBasis: Paul's stay of about three years at Ephesus (Acts 19:10; 20:31), after Corinth and the Gallio date.
summary: One of Paul's helpers, whom he sent with Timothy from Ephesus to Macedonia. Writing to Rome from Corinth, Paul sends greetings from Erastus, the city treasurer. In Paul's last letter, Erastus has stayed at Corinth.
body: Whether the three passages name one man is not certain.

later.text: A pavement at Corinth, laid in the first century, reads that Erastus laid it at his own expense in return for his aedileship. Some identify him with Paul's Erastus; others note that an aedile is not a treasurer. See the card on the inscription.

sources.title: Erastus inscription, Corinth (Kent, Corinth VIII.3 no. 232)
